verses.1: And that same year the people of Media rose up against them, and they gathered their armies to make war upon Israel. And the name of their king was Akrandes, and in the morning he assembled a great army from Syria, Cilicia, and Damascus.
verses.2: And he encamped by the crossing of the Jordan, and he sent messengers to Israel, saying, "Give me tribute of silver; and if not, I will come and take you captive, and I will plunder your goods, and I will carry away all your cattle, and I will take your children captive."
verses.3: "And I will exile you to a land you do not know, and there I will make you hewers of wood and drawers of water."
verses.4: "And do not trust in yourselves, saying, 'We are the people of God, and He is our Father who will protect us.' It is not God who has sent me to destroy you and to plunder your goods and all that is yours; it is to gather spoil that He has sent me."
verses.5: "Are there any whose gods have delivered them from foreign peoples whom I have taken captive, and whose goods and cattle I have plundered, and whom I have killed, and whose sons and children I have taken captive?"
verses.6: "So likewise will I do to you, unless you give me tribute as I have commanded you, and cross the Jordan, that I may plunder their goods and their cattle and take their wives captive."
verses.7: And when the children of Israel heard this, they wept bitterly before God, and they cried out and lamented and sought the one who would help them.
verses.8: And because of this, God gave strength to the three brothers, whose names were Mebqeyus, Meqabyos, and Yehuda, who were comely in appearance and mighty in all their strength.
verses.9: And when they heard the children of Israel weeping and wailing, their hearts were grieved, together with all the children of Israel, both men and women, and their priests and their princes, and all the house of Israel, men and women and children; all of them wept and cast dust upon their heads, and their nobles clothed themselves in sackcloth.
verses.10: And these brothers, comely and fair of appearance, resolved to go and to deliver them; and they took counsel and said, "Let us go and give our lives to death for the sake of these."
verses.11: And they went following one another, with their swords at their sides and their spears in their hands, and they went prepared, that they might be seen by the enemy.
verses.12: And they arrived while he was in the plain; and Mebqeyus stretched out his hand toward the enemy and struck his neck with one blow while the food was still in his mouth. And Yehuda and Meqabyos struck with the sword those who were at the right hand and at the left of their king.
verses.13: And when their king fell, they all fled and were scattered, and terror entered into their hearts, and their knees shook and their loins were loosened.
verses.14: And these brothers, comely and fair of appearance, were saved, and no one overtook them, nor did any harm befall them; but the wicked were cut down among them, for God brought punishment upon them.
verses.15: And they fell and died, and all who were with them were left behind until they crossed the Jordan, and all who were with them remained there. And when the children of Israel saw that they had fled, they went with their banners before them and took up their heads.
verses.16: And thus God delivered the children of Israel by the hand of Mebqeyus and his brothers.
verses.17: And the children of Israel dwelt in safety for many days, giving thanks to God.
verses.18: And after this they returned again to their place, and the children of Israel offered praise to God in purity. And again He blessed them with a people who were faithful, who tilled the fruit of their fields, and who planted trees and slept and raised their flocks and led their herds before them; and He did not withhold His deliverance from them, for they were a people who kept the law, because they always blessed God at all times.
